solver_selection.material_rows: kinds matrix, matrix_m7, phase_f, phase_f_v2, phase_r, workcell, postcut, phase4c, generalization and verify/e1: the runner wraps LiveCuttingMaterial.__init__ in its own process so that the material is built with solver = the arm solver (the frozen driver requested None (tlmpm_v4 by law) or "tlmpm_v5"); every redirect is recorded (requested -> effective) and the row is INVALID unless every material of the row was built with the arm solver and, for V6, position_update grid_musl_v1
solver_selection.direct_rows: verify/res and verify/probe build tlmpm_v5.TLMPM directly in the frozen drivers: the runner substitutes the arm class for that name inside its own process (the WP-12 V1-V4 verification mechanism), recorded as direct_import_substitution
solver_selection.labels: a frozen runner writes its own hard-coded solver label into its subdirectory result.json (e.g. "tlmpm_v5" or "tlmpm_v4"); the effective solver is the material receipt / bed module recorded in gridpos_result.json, which is authoritative
solver_selection.consequence: the V5 arm of the Phase F, matrix M9 and Phase R (a) style rows that WP-11 ran on tlmpm_v4 is a NEW tlmpm_v5 record (K = 1 packed codes equal ternary codes); the v4 records stand unchanged

setup.resolution: 1 mm particles / 4 mm grid / 0.1 ms material dt / 20 ms control dt unless a row states otherwise
setup.runtime_source: kinematic_ideal_tracking (measured_trajectory_material_replay for M9); no robot, grasp, slip, dynamics or cameras
setup.cut_diagnostics_v1: not attached (deviation from the decision skeleton): its step bracket wraps tlmpm_v5.TLMPM.step, which tlmpm_v6 overrides, so it would observe only the V5 arm; the per-control-step gridpos monitor below records the integrity and reported quantities for both arms alike
setup.monitor: gridpos_monitor_v1 (read-only, host copies after every control step of every LiveCuttingMaterial): finite x/v/F, min det F, max speed, labelled count per digit, blade/total reaction, tool work (stats[2]), blade overlap (stats[3]), fixture overlap (stats[0]), particle KE, grid KE (MUSL field), null-space KE (1/2 sum m |v_p - sum w v^MUSL|^2), min particle-centre local z on solid flat-board scenes; elastic energy (Hencky, F Fpi) every 10 control steps and at FINAL; FINAL piece (component) COM velocities; flip_drift_v1 grid-position residual |x - X - u_grid| (V6 expected < 1e-6 m at float32 rounding, reported)
setup.gpu: cuda:0 / cuda:1 shared with E2 and later Phase 5/7 runs: at most 2 jobs of this protocol at a time, one per GPU, a lane with < 6000 MiB free waits; other processes are never touched

CPU controls under grid_musl_v1: side push, flat press, blunt handle, no contact -> 0 labels, 1 component; armed stop and armed withdrawal -> labels unchanged, 1 component; half cut -> code-0 ligament below the stop
free block (no supports, no gravity, 2 mm lattice off the 4 mm node planes): per substep |Delta sum(m v) - blade impulse| < 1e-6 x total blade impulse, v5 and v6
v4/v5 law tests and the full CPU suite pass; frozen solver files unchanged (sha256)
S0_cpu.finding: the 4 mm CPU test block (blade_probe.block, s = dx) puts particles on node planes; zero-mass corners receive the stress-gradient term and the grid update drops it, so momentum is not conserved on that lattice in v4/v5 alike (pre-existing, not a v6 effect; formal 1 mm lattices sit at node fractions 1/8, 3/8, ... with no zero-weight corner). The momentum check therefore uses a 2 mm lattice

S1_kill.rule: Any S1 row FAIL -> v6 REJECTED: stop launching, keep every output, no tuning, write it up. A S1 row FAILs iff its V6 arm (either repeat) (a) does not PASS its frozen criterion, or (b) fails integrity, or (c) on a separating row has a different FINAL mechanical component count than the V5 arm, or (d) on a TRIM row has removal < 0.9 or substrate < 0.99, or (e) is INVALID/ERROR (solver selection not verified, crash). A V5-arm failure is recorded as a v5 finding and never excuses a V6 failure. The queue stops launching new rows on the first S1 FAIL (rows in flight finish and are kept); if the V5 arm of a failing row also fails, the report flags the row as not discriminating, but the S1 verdict is still FAIL.

S4_native.rule: needed only before any Native use of v6; not scheduled in this protocol execution (NOT_RUN unless a later decision schedules it). Criteria: Phase 2b criteria (workcell_live_v1), HOME return, per-step wall <= 1.2x the Phase 2b per-step wall

det F > 0 and min det F > 0.5 over the episode
no particle centre below the board top (solid flat-board scenes: workcell FB_*, E1 A/R rows, phase4c; not slotted D rows, legacy trays or segment boards)

equal FINAL mechanical component count to the V5 arm on separating rows

an S2/S3 acceptance row whose frozen criterion FAILs on V6 AND on the V5 arm at the same commit is not attributable to v6: it is reported as PASS_V5_ALSO_FAILS (never hidden), the stage verdict becomes PASS_WITH_V5_FAILURES and the reviewer decides; this does not apply to S1 (every S1 failure kills)
gates.verdict_order: PASS > PASS_NONFORMAL > FAIL > ERROR/INVALID; for E1 outcome labels SEPARATED > CONNECTED; known-failure rows compare their class
not_gated_reported: blade force (steady mean, window), tool work, blade/fixture overlap
particle / grid / null-space KE, elastic energy

gates.envelope_note: a change in a reported quantity is a question for a new envelope version, never a re-score of envelope v1
gates.decision: ACCEPTED iff S0-S3 gates pass (decision_by_gates ACCEPTED_BY_GATES, or ACCEPTED_BY_GATES_V5_FAILURES_TO_REVIEW when only non-attributable rows failed); otherwise REJECTED (kept). The xhigh reviewer accepts or rejects; this protocol only computes the gates.
gates.trim_numbers: TRIM rows read removal / substrate from the FINAL-state values of their own evaluator (minimum over the selected items and over equivalent keys; mid-episode END_* states and unselected protrusions excluded); a TRIM row without such numbers falls back to its frozen verdict
